title: Toeplitz Block Mixing for Scalable Multi-Head Linear Attention

contributions.purpose: Shows that the full M x M block mixing matrix in Multi-Head Linear Attention (MHLA) is over-parameterized.
contributions.mechanism: Fits the learned MHLA mixing matrices to a distance-tied (translation-invariant) kernel to show coefficients depend primarily on relative block distance.
contributions.evaluation: Distance-tied kernel fit yields R^2 > 0.995 across all layers.
contributions.source_quote: We show that Dense MHLA learns approximately Toeplitz mixing patterns (R^2 > 0.995 across all layers), suggesting the full M x M parameterization is unnecessary.

contributions.purpose: Removes the O(M^2) block-mixing bottleneck of MHLA and enables extrapolation to longer sequences.
contributions.mechanism: Toeplitz Block Mixing (TBM) parameterizes the mixing kernel as a mixture of exponentials K(delta) = sum_r a_r exp(-lambda_r delta), constraining mixing to depend only on block distance.
contributions.evaluation: Reduces mixing complexity from O(M^2 d^2) to O(M R d^2) for kernel rank R << M and supports length extrapolation since the kernel is defined for any distance.
contributions.source_quote: We propose TBM, a Toeplitz-constrained parameterization that reduces mixing complexity from O(M^2 d^2) to O(M R d^2) and enables length extrapolation.

contributions.purpose: Validates that the Toeplitz constraint improves both accuracy and throughput on recall-intensive tasks.
contributions.mechanism: Compares TBM to Dense MHLA on associative recall tasks and runs ablations over kernel rank R.
contributions.evaluation: TBM achieves 7.3x higher accuracy than Dense MHLA (1.25% vs 0.17%) with 1.24x throughput improvement, extrapolates to 8x longer sequences, and ablations show even R=1 (single exponential) suffices.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that TBM achieves 7.3x higher accuracy than Dense MHLA while being 1.24x faster, with ablations showing that even R = 1 (single exponential) suffices.

self_declared_provenance.quote: However, these methods introduce O(M^2) complexity in the number of heads M and cannot extrapolate to sequence lengths beyond training. Our work addresses both limitations through Toeplitz-constrained mixing.
Our work differs by discovering that the mixing patterns learned by MHLA are inherently Toeplitz, motivating a principled parameterization that reduces complexity while enabling extrapolation.

notes: Headline accuracy numbers are very low in absolute terms (1.25% vs 0.17% on associative recall); the 7.3x claim is a ratio of two near-zero accuracies.
